metadata.title: feat: Rust MCP runtime pre-invoke plugin hooks and WXO auth support
metadata.author: jonpspri

description:
## Summary

- Add pre-tool hook plugin capability to the Rust MCP runtime, enabling plugins (e.g. WXO connections) to inject credentials and transform arguments on the Rust direct execution path
- Extract `run_pre_request_hooks()` as a shared function so both the Python middleware chain and the Rust internal auth path run identical HTTP_PRE_REQUEST plugin hooks
- Add `plugins_can_override_auth_headers` config setting (default `false`) to guard against plugins overwriting inbound auth headers unless explicitly trusted
- Disable plan caching when pre-invoke hooks ran, since hook results depend on per-call context
- Extend load test with multi-tenant identity and WXO auth JWT claims
- Document the two-phase resolve-then-execute model, plugin execution by mode, and direct execution eligibility

## Test plan

- [x] Existing `TestRustMcpExecutionPlan` tests pass with updated fallback reason
- [x] WebSocket transport test updated for scoped log capture
- [x] HTTP auth middleware tests pass
- [x] Ruff and bandit pass on all changed files
- [ ] Integration test with WXO plugin enabled (manual/CI)
- [ ] Load test with multi-tenant JWT claims against deployed stack

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body: EchoDelayUser falls back to BEARER_TOKEN when WXO_AUTH_ENABLED is false, but if MCPGATEWAY_BEARER_TOKEN isn’t set this silently proceeds without an Authorization header (and the load test will fail in a less obvious way). Consider failing fast here with a clear error when WXO_AUTH_ENABLED is false and BEARER_TOKEN is empty, mirroring the previous _get_auth_token() behavior.

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body: NUM_TENANTS is used to build TENANT_IDS and then random.choice(TENANT_IDS). If NUM_TENANTS is set to 0 (or negative) this will raise at runtime in a non-obvious place. Add a small validation after parsing NUM_TENANTS to enforce >= 1 with a clear error message.

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body: ToolHookType.TOOL_PRE_INVOKE is invoked with headers built from the inbound request (hook_headers = request_headers), but in the normal invoke_tool() flow the pre-invoke hook receives the outbound headers that will be sent upstream (gateway/tool auth + passthrough). This mismatch can break plugins that expect to see/modify the actual upstream header set. Consider passing the computed outbound header dict (runtime_headers/headers) into ToolPreInvokePayload.headers instead of request_headers, then applying the modified headers back onto runtime_headers case-insensitively.

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body: In prepare_rust_mcp_tool_execution(), the pre-invoke hook’s modified_payload.name is being applied to remoteToolName (via tool_name_original). In the normal Python invoke_tool() path, ToolPreInvokePayload.name mutations do not affect the upstream MCP tool name (call_tool uses tool_name_original computed from DB), so this changes behavior between Rust-direct and Python fallback. To keep parity, either ignore modified_payload.name here (and only apply modified args/headers), or update the Python execution path so that tool_name_original used for the upstream call is also updated when pre-invoke modifies the name (with corresponding tests).

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body: runtime_headers/plugin_headers merging is currently case-sensitive (e.g., existing "Authorization" plus plugin-provided "authorization" will both be emitted). When Rust deserializes the JSON object into a HashMap and then builds a HeaderMap, iteration order is nondeterministic, so the effective auth header value can be flaky. Normalize header names case-insensitively before merging (e.g., lower-case keys), and ensure plugin-provided values deterministically override prior values when intended.

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body: run_pre_request_hooks() merges headers with a plain dict spread ({**headers, **modified_headers_dict}). Because HTTP headers are case-insensitive, this can yield duplicate logical headers when only casing differs (e.g., "Authorization" vs "authorization"); when written back to request.scope["headers"], this becomes multiple ASGI header entries with the same lowercased name and ambiguous precedence. Consider normalizing keys (lowercasing) for both input + plugin headers before applying the override guard and merging, so there is exactly one value per header name and plugin overrides behave deterministically when enabled.

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body: The overridden-header check recomputes `{h.lower() for h in headers}` inside the set comprehension, which is unnecessary work and makes the logic harder to read. Precompute the inbound lowercased header-name set once (e.g., original_lower = {h.lower() for h in headers}) and reuse it when determining which auth-protected headers were overridden.

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body: _run_internal_mcp_authentication() uses the raw string literal "http_pre_request" in has_hooks_for(). Elsewhere the codebase consistently uses HttpHookType.HTTP_PRE_REQUEST; using the constant avoids typos and keeps refactors safer (the hook type is a public API surface for plugins).

comments.author: jonpspri
comments.body: Agreed. Added a fail-fast `RuntimeError` when `WXO_AUTH_ENABLED=false` and `BEARER_TOKEN` is empty, mirroring the previous `_get_auth_token()` behavior. Fixed in 50aa249.

comments.author: jonpspri
comments.body: Agreed. Added a `ValueError` guard enforcing `NUM_TENANTS >= 1` at module load time. Fixed in 50aa249.

comments.author: jonpspri
comments.body: Good catch. The Python `invoke_tool()` path passes the computed outbound headers (gateway auth + passthrough) into the pre-invoke hook, but this code was passing the inbound `request_headers`. Changed to pass `runtime_headers` (which already has gateway auth, OAuth tokens, and passthrough headers applied) for parity. Fixed in 50aa249.

comments.author: jonpspri
comments.body: This finding is incorrect. The Python `invoke_tool()` path **does** apply tool name changes from pre-invoke hooks — see `tool_service.py:3704`: `name = payload.name`. Both paths already have the same behavior, so no change is needed.

comments.author: jonpspri
comments.body: Agreed. Plugin-provided header keys are now lowercased on merge (`runtime_headers[str(hk).lower()] = str(hv)`) to ensure deterministic override behavior regardless of casing. Fixed in 50aa249.

comments.author: jonpspri
comments.body: Agreed. Both the original and plugin-provided headers are now normalized to lowercase keys before merging, preventing duplicate logical headers from casing differences. Fixed in 50aa249.

comments.author: jonpspri
comments.body: Agreed. Precomputed `original_lower = {h.lower() for h in headers}` once and reused it in the override check. Fixed in 50aa249.

comments.author: jonpspri
comments.body: Agreed. Changed to `HttpHookType.HTTP_PRE_REQUEST` and merged the import with the existing `from mcpgateway.plugins.framework import ...` line. Fixed in 50aa249.

commits.message:
feat: run pre-request plugin hooks on Rust MCP auth path

Extract run_pre_request_hooks() from HttpAuthMiddleware into a shared
function and call it from _run_internal_mcp_authentication() so that
HTTP_PRE_REQUEST plugins (e.g. WXO auth token exchange) fire on the
Rust MCP ingress path, not just the Python middleware chain.

test: add coverage for run_pre_request_hooks and pre-invoke hook execution

Add 15 new tests covering previously untested code paths:

TestRunPreRequestHooks (9 tests):
- No hooks registered returns original headers unchanged
- Plugin-modified headers are merged correctly
- No modification when plugin returns no payload
- Auth header override stripped by default (deny path)
- Auth header override allowed when plugins_can_override_auth_headers=True
- Exception in hook returns original headers safely
- Merged headers normalized to lowercase keys
- GlobalContext created when not provided
- Provided GlobalContext reused

TestRustMcpExecutionPlan (6 tests):
- Post-invoke hooks force fallback (using side_effect for hook type branching)
- Active trace forces fallback
- Pre-invoke only returns eligible plan with hasPreInvokeHooks and modifiedArgs
- Pre-invoke hook can rename tool in plan
- No hook fields in plan when no pre-invoke hooks registered
- Pre-invoke hook receives outbound runtime headers, not inbound request headers

commits.message:
fix: auth-header override guard bypass with mixed-case keys

The `overridden` set stored original-case plugin header keys, but the
filter compared lowercased keys against it. A plugin returning
"Authorization" (mixed-case) instead of "authorization" would bypass
the plugins_can_override_auth_headers=false guard and overwrite inbound
auth headers.

Fix: normalize `overridden` to lowercase so the filter comparison is
case-insensitive. Add a deny-path test for mixed-case auth headers.

Also document the known limitation that pre-invoke hooks may run twice
when Rust direct execution fails and falls back to the Python path.
Pre-invoke plugins must be idempotent for correctness on this path.

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
commits.author: Mihai Criveti

commits.message:
fix: plugin context parity and double pre-invoke on Rust fallback

Two issues addressed:

1. Context parity: prepare_rust_mcp_tool_execution() now accepts
   plugin_global_context and plugin_context_table from the resolve
   handler, reusing the middleware-provided GlobalContext (which carries
   JWT claims state, correlation ID, and user identity). Tool/gateway
   metadata is injected before pre-invoke hooks run, matching the
   invoke_tool() pattern. The resolve handler extracts these from
   request.state and passes them through.

2. Double pre-invoke prevention: When Rust direct execution fails and
   falls back to /_internal/mcp/tools/call, Rust now injects an
   x-contextforge-pre-invoke-ran header. invoke_tool() checks for this
   header and skips re-running TOOL_PRE_INVOKE hooks, preventing double
   execution for non-idempotent plugins (rate limiters, token exchange,
   audit hooks).

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
commits.author: Mihai Criveti

commits.message:
fix: prevent external callers from spoofing x-contextforge-pre-invoke-ran

The skip_pre_invoke flag was derived from raw request headers, which
meant any external client could send x-contextforge-pre-invoke-ran:true
to bypass TOOL_PRE_INVOKE security/policy plugins.

Fix: replace header-based derivation with an explicit skip_pre_invoke
parameter threaded through _execute_rpc_tools_call() → invoke_tool().
Only the trusted internal /_internal/mcp/tools/call endpoint (which is
authenticated via shared-secret and not exposed to external clients)
reads the header and sets the flag. The public RPC path never sets it.

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
commits.author: Mihai Criveti

commits.message:
fix: update test_rpc_tool_invocation for skip_pre_invoke parameter
